title: IVF: embryo transfer
what: The doctor places an embryo into the womb through a thin, soft tube. It is quick, with no cuts, and usually without anesthesia.
why: It is a key step of IVF. After the eggs are collected and fertilized, the embryo is placed in the womb so it can attach.
duration: the transfer itself usually takes 5 to 15 minutes; you are at the clinic for about 1 to 2 hours
tell_doctor: All the medicines and hormones you use
If you have pain low in the belly, bloating, or bloody spotting

prepare.title: Hormones
prepare.text: Keep taking your support medicines exactly as your doctor planned. Do not change anything on your own.

prepare.title: Bladder
prepare.text: You are often asked to come with a moderately full bladder. It helps the ultrasound view. Your clinic will tell you how much to drink.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: A light breakfast is usually fine. If sedation is planned, ask how long not to eat.

prepare.title: On the day
prepare.text: No perfume or strong-smelling cosmetics. Wear comfortable clothes.

bring: Socks. The room may be cool
Someone with you, if you like
steps: You are invited into the room, and your name and embryo details are checked
You lie on the gynecology chair
The doctor puts in a speculum, as in a usual exam, and cleans the cervix
The embryologist hands over a thin tube with the embryo
Using ultrasound, the doctor passes it into the womb and releases the embryo
The tube is checked under a microscope to make sure the embryo stayed in the womb
You rest lying down for a few minutes, then you can go
feel: It usually feels like a gynecology exam or a smear test
Sometimes a mild cramp low in the belly
A full bladder is uncomfortable. You can go to the toilet right after the transfer. The embryo will not fall out
after: Strict bed rest is not needed. Just live a normal, calm life
You are usually advised to avoid saunas, hot baths, and heavy exercise. Check with your doctor
Keep taking your hormone support exactly as planned
A blood pregnancy test is usually done after 9 to 14 days. Your clinic will tell you when
A home test taken too early can be wrong
red_flags: Severe belly pain, heavy bleeding, or a fever: see a doctor right away
Severe bloating, shortness of breath, sudden weight gain, or peeing very little: see a doctor urgently or call emergency services

faq.q: Do I need to lie down after embryo transfer?
faq.a: No. Long bed rest does not raise the chance of pregnancy. A calm routine is enough.

faq.q: Can the embryo fall out if I go to the toilet?
faq.a: No. The embryo is inside the womb and has no connection with the bladder.

faq.q: When can I find out if it worked?
faq.a: Usually after 9 to 14 days, with an hCG blood test. A test taken too early often gives a wrong result.

reminders.text: Embryo transfer tomorrow. Keep taking your hormones as planned. Bring your documents and socks.
Transfer soon. If your clinic asked, drink water so your bladder is moderately full.
